evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: The user wants to run `cargo test --workspace` (takes ~8 minutes) in the background so they can immediately ask questions about another module without blocking the session. How should you launch and track it?
evals.expected_output: Launch the command in the background (using host `run_in_background`, Bash `{ trap '' HUP; ...; } </dev/null >"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &`, or PowerShell `Start-Process -PassThru` with `-EncodedCommand`), verify startup after 1 second, report the literal `BG_PID`/`shell_id` and `LOG_FILE` concisely, and end the turn immediately so the user can ask questions. Piggyback non-blocking status checks on subsequent user turns.
assertions: Launches the command in the background without blocking the foreground turn
Ends the turn after reporting PID or shell_id so the session stays responsive
Piggybacks non-blocking status checks on subsequent user turns

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: The user asks to run a data migration script in the background and automatically report progress every 15 seconds while they are idle, while keeping the task safe if they interrupt to ask a question. How should you implement the polling?
evals.expected_output: Launch the migration detached in the background, then execute one bounded 15-second wait-and-check per tool call (exiting early if the process finishes via `kill -0` loop in Bash or `$p.WaitForExit(15000)` in PowerShell), emit a brief progress update between tool calls, and repeat until completion. Never loop until completion inside a single shell call, and note that interrupting the turn leaves the detached OS process running.
assertions: Uses one bounded wait-and-check per tool call rather than an in-shell loop until completion
Emits visible progress updates between tool calls
Caps log inspection (`tail -n` or `Get-Content -Tail`) instead of reading full logs
Preserves the detached background process if the user interrupts the turn

evals.prompt: Offline reasoning only, do not execute commands: Why do `python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(60)' &` in Bash and `Start-Job` in PowerShell fail or block in CLI agent tool calls, and what quote-safe patterns should be used instead on both platforms?
evals.expected_output: In Bash, a raw `&` inherits open stdout/stderr/stdin pipes so the tool runner blocks waiting for EOF, and wrapping with `sh -c '...'` breaks when the command contains single quotes; use a command group `{ trap '' HUP; <command>; ...; } </dev/null >"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &` instead. In PowerShell, `Start-Job` runs inside the current PowerShell session and terminates as soon as the tool call's subshell exits; use `Start-Process -PassThru` with `-EncodedCommand`, `-RedirectStandardOutput`/`-RedirectStandardError`, and `-WindowStyle Hidden` to create a quote-safe independent OS process.
assertions: Identifies inherited stdout/stderr/stdin pipes as the cause of Bash tool runner blocking
Explains that PowerShell `Start-Job` dies when the tool call's session exits
Recommends `Start-Process -PassThru` with redirected output on PowerShell/Windows
